title: Housing policy events
note: Acts, statutory instruments, programmes and institutions. The mark is Royal Assent for an Act, the made date for an instrument, and the start date for a programme or institution. Commencement, announcement and repeal are separate facts. An overlapping statistic is context, not an effect.

eras.label: Before 1900
eras.focus: Sanitary law and the first powers to clear and rebuild unhealthy districts.
A health ministry, state subsidy for council building and interwar slum clearance.
Post-war new towns, national planning control and a housing ministry.
Housing associations, rent and leasehold reform, improvement areas and homelessness duties.
Right to buy, consolidation of housing law and new tenancy types.
Devolved housing law, conditions standards, national agencies and grant programmes.

eras.label: 2020–present
eras.focus: Building safety, social housing regulation, leasehold and tenancy reform.

events.title: Artizans and Labourers Dwellings Improvement Act 1875
events.summary: Let local authorities in large towns make improvement schemes for areas of unhealthy dwellings, with compulsory purchase. Royal Assent is printed as 29 June 1875.
events.extent: No single extent section was found in the enacted PDF. The text names the metropolis, urban sanitary districts in England of 25,000 people or more, and urban sanitary districts in Ireland. Ireland was then part of the United Kingdom and is not mapped to Northern Ireland here. Scotland is not named as an area.
events.status_note: legislation.gov.uk serves the original enacted text only. Later amendment or repeal is not recorded here.

events.title: Public Health Act 1875
events.summary: Consolidated and amended the public health law for England. Royal Assent is printed as 11 August 1875. It is recorded here because housing conditions were dealt with through sanitary law before housing Acts existed; the sections on dwellings are not extracted.
events.extent: Section 2: the Act does not extend to Scotland or Ireland, nor to the metropolis except where it says so. At the time 'England' in statutes included Wales.
events.status_note: legislation.gov.uk serves a revised text and does not mark the Act repealed. Provisions may since have been amended, repealed or left uncommenced; they are not checked one by one here.

events.title: Housing of the Working Classes Act 1890
events.summary: Consolidated and amended the Acts on artizans' and labourers' dwellings and the housing of the working classes. Royal Assent is printed as 18 August 1890.
events.extent: The enacted PDF applies the Act to Scotland with modifications (some provisions, such as Part II county council powers, do not apply there) and applies a schedule to Ireland with modifications. Ireland is not mapped to Northern Ireland here.
events.status_note: legislation.gov.uk serves the original enacted text only. Later amendment or repeal is not recorded here.

events.title: Ministry of Health
events.summary: The ministry created in 1919 that took over health and local government powers in England and Wales, including housing, until housing passed to a new minister in 1951.
events.extent: England and Wales, per the long title of the 1919 Act.
events.date_note: Start: Royal Assent of the Ministry of Health Act 1919, which established the Ministry. The Orders in Council that transferred powers are not pinned. End: not pinned; housing functions moved in 1951.
events.status_note: Housing and local government functions were transferred by an Order in Council dated 29 January 1951 (SI 1951/142), per the Commons debate of 22 February 1951. The Ministry itself continued for health.

sources.label: Commons debate on the transfer of functions, 22 February 1951

events.title: Ministry of Health Act 1919
events.summary: Established a Ministry of Health to exercise powers on health and local government in England and Wales. Royal Assent is printed as 3 June 1919. Powers moved to the Minister on days appointed by Order in Council.
events.extent: The long title limits the Ministry's health and local government powers to England and Wales, with some powers for the Chief Secretary in Ireland. legislation.gov.uk gives the extent of the revised text as E+W+S+N.I.

commencements.scope: Not pinned. Section 11 brings the Act into operation on days appointed by Order in Council; the transfer of powers to the Minister was to be no later than one year after passing.

events.status_note: legislation.gov.uk titles the revised text 'Ministry of Health Act 1919 (repealed)'. The repealing enactment is not recorded here.

events.title: Housing, Town Planning, &c. Act 1919
events.summary: The short title on the enacted text is the Housing, Town Planning, &c. Act, 1919. Royal Assent is printed there as 31 July 1919. Addison Act is a later name, not the short title. The duties in the sections are not extracted in this anchor.
events.extent: Section 51 of the enacted text: the Act does not extend to Scotland or Ireland. Do not read the Act as the housing law of Scotland; see the Housing, Town Planning, &c. (Scotland) Act 1919.
events.status_note: legislation.gov.uk currently serves the original enacted text only. A later repeal is not recorded here.

events.title: Ministry of Housing and Local Government
aliases: Minister of Local Government and Planning
events.summary: The minister who took over housing and local government from the Minister of Health in 1951, first styled Minister of Local Government and Planning and renamed Housing and Local Government later that year.
events.extent: Functions transferred from the Minister of Health, whose powers covered England and Wales.
events.date_note: Start: the date of the Transfer of Functions (Minister of Health and Minister of Local Government and Planning) (No. 1) Order 1951, as given in the Commons. Its coming-into-force day is not pinned. The renaming to Housing and Local Government was confirmed in the Commons on 12 November 1951. End: dissolved by the Secretary of State for the Environment Order 1970.
events.status_note: Article 2 of SI 1970/1681 dissolves the Ministry of Housing and Local Government.

events.title: Housing Act 1980
events.summary: Royal Assent is printed as 8 August 1980. Part I Chapter I of the enacted text gives a secure tenant the right to buy the freehold of a house, or a long lease of a flat, in the circumstances that Chapter sets out. Section 1(7) points to a separate Scottish right to purchase in the Tenants' Rights, Etc. (Scotland) Act 1980 (1980 c. 52). Commencement No. 1 did not appoint Part I.
events.extent: The revised text on legislation.gov.uk records that the whole Act was repealed for Scotland by the Housing (Scotland) Act 1987. Part I is not that Scottish right to purchase.

commencements.scope: Does not appoint Part I. Section 121 comes into operation on 1 October 1980. The Schedule comes into operation on 3 October 1980. The order that appoints Chapter I of Part I is not yet in this registry.

events.status_note: legislation.gov.uk carries a revised text with later effects. The right-to-buy commencement date is deliberately blank.

events.title: Renters' Rights Act 2025
events.summary: Royal Assent is printed as 27 October 2025. The long title includes abolishing fixed-term assured tenancies and assured shorthold tenancies. Those provisions were not in force on Royal Assent. Commencement No. 2 appoints Chapter 1 of Part 1, except section 25(3), for 1 May 2026, and only for assured tenancies that are not social housing assured tenancies.
events.extent: The commencement instrument is titled Landlord and Tenant, England. Explanatory notes, which are department text and not the Act, say the Act's extent is England and Wales with some provisions extending to Scotland, and that application is mostly England. Social housing assured tenancies can have a different commencement day under section 145(8).

commencements.scope: Chapter 1 of Part 1, except section 25(3), for assured tenancies that are not social housing assured tenancies. Made 16 April 2026. England.

events.status_note: Checked 5 November 2026. The 1 May 2026 appointment covers private assured tenancies only. It is not the whole Act.
